standard_prerequisites.name: Two-sided glueing of one-dimensional semi-local rings
standard_prerequisites.use: Performs the induction step that combines one local ring with the intersection of the others.

core_obligations: Take A = A_1 cap ... cap A_r and prove property (3) first: a closed point lying in two of the open pieces would force the map A_i tensor A_j -> K to land in the local ring A_m (proof lines 7524-7528).
Argue by induction on r for properties (1) and (2): for r > 1 the induction hypothesis applies to the intersection B = A_2 cap ... cap A_r (proof lines 7529-7531).
Apply the two-sided semi-local lemma to the pair A_1 and B to obtain the open immersion and covering statements for A = A_1 cap B (proof lines 7531-7533).
proof_roadmap: Define the candidate ring as the intersection.
Handle the disjointness of closed points first.
Induct on the number of rings using the two-sided glueing lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs, from finitely many one-dimensional Noetherian semi-local subrings A_i of a field K with A_i tensor A_j mapping onto K for i not equal to j, a Noetherian semi-local domain A inside all of them such that the spectra of the A_i are open subschemes covering Spec(A) with each closed point lying in exactly one of them. The proof takes A to be the intersection of the A_i, derives property (3) from the surjectivity hypothesis by noting that a common closed point would force A_i tensor A_j -> K to land in A_m, and then proves (1) and (2) by induction on r, applying the two-sided semi-local lemma to A = A_1 cap B where B is the intersection of the remaining rings (proof lines 7524-7533). H2: the intersection construction together with the induction through the two-sided lemma is the substance.
